title: TARNet: Task-Aware Reconstruction for Time-Series Transformer

problem.claim: Time-series representation learning should use temporal order information to support predictive end tasks such as classification and regression.

gap.claim: Existing masked reconstruction pre-training decouples reconstruction from the end task, so learned representations may be sub-optimal because timestamp importance varies across tasks.

contributions.claim: TARNet uses Transformers for task-aware time-series reconstruction to augment end-task performance.
A data-driven masking strategy uses end-task self-attention score distributions to sample important timestamps for reconstruction.
The reconstruction and end tasks are trained alternately each epoch in one parameter-sharing model.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe TARNet as a new model for task-aware data reconstruction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on tens of classification and regression datasets reportedly show that TARNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models across all evaluation metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal order information can guide representation learning for predictive time-series tasks.
Prior approaches reconstruct randomly masked time segments before fine-tuning and report improved end-task performance.
This paradigm separates reconstruction from the end task and may learn task-uninformed, sub-optimal representations.
TARNet selects task-important timestamps using end-task attention, reconstructs them, and alternates reconstruction with end-task training.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across all evaluation metrics on tens of classification and regression datasets.

source_observation.claim: Timestamp importance can vary significantly across end tasks.

interpretation.claim: Representation-learning objectives may benefit from conditioning their training signal on the downstream task.

application.claim: Use downstream-task signals to prioritize which temporal elements receive reconstruction or auxiliary-learning emphasis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether task-aware masking helps when attention scores are poorly calibrated or when downstream tasks are unavailable during representation learning.

unknowns: The specific datasets, baseline identities, metric names, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, or implementation details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance.
